title: Internationalization
lead: A multilingual memory: 14 UI locales, 100+ embedding languages, non-Latin entities.
summary: MemPalace localizes UI and entity detection across 14 languages via JSON catalogs in mempalace/i18n/. The loader handles case-insensitive BCP 47 tags, dotted-key interpolation, and language-aware entity patterns. Non-Latin scripts are kept intact through script-aware word boundaries that account for combining marks Python's \b drops. An optional multilingual embeddinggemma-300m model (0.88 cross-lingual cosine similarity) drops in beside the English-only all-MiniLM default.

concepts.definition: Standardized language code (RFC 5646), case-insensitive; MemPalace normalizes via _canonical_lang() so PT-BR, pt-br, Pt-Br all map to the same file.

Non-spacing diacritical mark (Unicode categories Mc/Mn) like Hindi matra (ा) or Arabic vowel (َ); Python's \b word boundary ignores them, causing truncation. MemPalace fixes this via script-aware lookaround boundaries.
Regex lookaround ((?<=[chars])(?=[^chars])) that treats declared character ranges (e.g. Devanagari U+0900-U+097F) as word-internal, preserving combining marks and multi-codepoint names.
Language-specific regex sets for candidate_patterns, person_verb_patterns, dialogue_patterns, project_verb_patterns, pronouns, stopwords; merged per-language via get_entity_patterns().

ChromaDB-compatible callable returning vector embeddings. Two choices: minilm (384-dim, English-only, faster) or embeddinggemma (384-dim via Matryoshka truncation, multilingual, 0.88 cross-lingual cosine similarity).
Training technique allowing embedding models to produce useful outputs at any dimensionality. EmbeddinggemmaONNX truncates 768-dim output to 384-dim to be a drop-in ChromaDB replacement.
Localized compression instruction stored in each locale's i18n JSON (e.g. Japanese vs English version), consumed by Dialect.compress() to guide LLM-based lossy summarization.
_entity_cache dict keyed on tuple(languages); caches merged entity patterns to avoid recompiling across get_entity_patterns() calls.

symbols.name: load_lang
symbols.role: Loads a language dictionary from JSON, stores globally, and returns the dict. Falls back to English if language not found.

symbols.name: t
symbols.role: Retrieves a localized string by dotted key (e.g., 'cli.mine_complete') and performs variable interpolation with kwargs.

symbols.name: get_entity_patterns
symbols.role: Merges entity-detection patterns (candidate_patterns, person_verb_patterns, etc.) from one or more locales, applies script-aware boundary expansion, and returns a cached dict.

symbols.name: _script_boundary
symbols.role: Generates a lookaround-based word boundary regex that treats a declared character class as word-internal, preserving combining marks.

symbols.name: EmbeddinggemmaONNX
symbols.role: ChromaDB-compatible embedding function using onnx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-ONNX, supporting 100+ languages with 0.88 cross-lingual cosine similarity.

symbols.name: get_embedding_function
symbols.role: Factory returning a cached embedding function (EmbeddinggemmaONNX or minilm) for the requested device and model.

symbols.name: _resolve_providers
symbols.role: Maps device names to ONNX Runtime execution provider lists, with fallback to CPU and one-shot warnings for unavailable accelerators.

symbols.name: Dialect
symbols.role: AAAK Dialect encoder accepting a language parameter; loads language-specific AAAK instruction and regex patterns to guide lossy text compression.

symbols.name: extract_candidates
symbols.role: Extracts capitalized proper noun candidates from text using language-aware patterns, returning {name: frequency} for candidates appearing 3+ times.

symbols.name: detect_entities
symbols.role: Scans files, extracts candidates, scores and classifies them as person/project/uncertain, returning a dict with optional agent_personas bucket.

symbols.name: _canonical_lang
symbols.role: Resolves mixed-case language codes (PT-BR, pt-br) to canonical on-disk filename stems via case-insensitive globbing.

symbols.name: available_languages
symbols.role: Returns sorted list of all available language codes by globbing *.json in the i18n directory.

surprises.title: Python's \b Silently Truncates Names with Combining Marks
surprises.detail: \b is a transition between \w (Unicode Letter/Number) and non-\w, but Unicode Marks (category Mc/Mn) are non-\w. So अनीता at a word boundary becomes अनीत if \b is used literally. MemPalace's solution—script-aware lookaround boundaries—is elegant but non-obvious.

surprises.title: 14 Languages But Only 3 Have Full Entity Patterns
surprises.detail: Only zh-CN, hi, and ko declare boundary_chars and full entity sections. ja.json and pt-br.json have no entity section, so they fall back to English patterns. Most locales translate UI strings but reuse English entity detection.

surprises.title: Multilingual Embeddings Trade Speed for Quality
surprises.detail: EmbeddinggemmaONNX achieves 0.88 cross-lingual cosine similarity (vs MiniLM's 0.35) but is slower: 300MB lazy-downloaded model, slower tokenizer, higher inference cost. Onboarding defaults to embeddinggemma for new users but existing palaces use minilm for backward compatibility.

surprises.title: Entity Cache Shares Across Different Case Variants
surprises.detail: get_entity_patterns() normalizes language codes to canonical form before cache lookup, so (PT-BR, en) and (pt-br, en) hit the same cache entry, reducing redundant merges.

surprises.title: EmbeddinggemmaONNX Persists Its Name in ChromaDB Collections
surprises.detail: The name() method returns 'embeddinggemma_300m', and ChromaDB persists this on the collection. Switching models without rebuilding makes ChromaDB reject the old collection on name mismatch—intentional, forcing 'mempalace repair rebuild-index', but surprising.

designDecisions.decision: Localize UI strings and entity patterns in a single JSON structure per language.
designDecisions.rationale: Keeps all locale-specific data (UI, entity patterns, boundary_chars, AAAK instructions) colocated and in one schema. Avoids spreading definitions across multiple files and makes it clear what's translatable vs what's structural.

designDecisions.decision: Default multilingual embeddings (embeddinggemma) for new palaces, but preserve minilm for backward compatibility.
designDecisions.rationale: 0.88 cross-lingual cosine similarity is a major quality win for non-English content, but existing palaces were built with minilm's vector space. Switching requires reindexing, so onboarding offers embeddinggemma as default and recommends it, but doesn't break existing users.

designDecisions.decision: Script-aware word boundaries via lookaround, not post-processing.
designDecisions.rationale: Baking boundary logic into the regex pattern itself avoids slicing/truncating extracted names after the fact. Names with combining marks are matched correctly the first time, not cleaned up later.

designDecisions.decision: Lazy-load EmbeddinggemmaONNX model on first use, not at import time.
designDecisions.rationale: The 300MB model should not block CLI startup or onboarding. Lazy loading lets CPU-only users run MemPalace without forced GPU dependencies, and keeps import overhead minimal even when the model isn't used.

designDecisions.decision: Cache entity patterns by canonical language tuple, allowing mixed case in callers.
designDecisions.rationale: BCP 47 tags are case-insensitive per RFC. Normalizing before cache lookup lets callers pass any capitalization and still share cached merged patterns, reducing redundant regex compilation.

related.why: Entity detection patterns in i18n drive the entity system; entity_detector.py directly calls get_entity_patterns().
AAAK Dialect is localized via i18n; each locale's aaak.instruction guides lossy compression.
Multilingual embeddings (embeddinggemma vs minilm) are used for semantic search and knowledge graph queries.
ChromaDB collections persist embedding function names; switching embedding models requires rebuild-index.
CLI messages (mine_start, search_no_results, etc.) are all localized via i18n t() function.
Entity detection during mining uses get_entity_patterns() with entity_languages from config.

searchDoc.title: Internationalization
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace localizes UI and entity detection across 14 languages via JSON catalogs in mempalace/i18n/, with case-insensitive BCP 47 tags, script-aware word boundaries for combining marks, and optional multilingual embeddinggemma-300m embeddings.
searchDoc.body: MemPalace's internationalization layer localizes both UI strings and entity detection across 14 languages: en, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, de, es, fr, pt-br, it, ru, hi, id, and be. Each language is one JSON catalog under mempalace/i18n/ that serves two purposes at once: UI strings (terms, CLI messages, AAAK compression instruction) and entity-detection patterns (candidate patterns, person verb patterns, boundary characters). The loader, load_lang, reads a locale file after normalizing the requested BCP 47 tag through _canonical_lang, which lowercases and glob-matches so PT-BR, pt-br, and Pt-Br all resolve to the same on-disk file. The t function looks up dotted keys like cli.mine_complete, interpolates kwargs, and falls back to the key or English when a string is missing. A central problem this area solves is non-Latin script support. Python's built-in word boundary, backslash-b, is a transition between word characters and non-word characters, but Unicode combining marks such as Hindi matras and Arabic vowels are not word characters. As a result a literal boundary truncates names like अनीता to अनीत. The _script_boundary function builds a lookaround-based boundary that treats locale-declared boundary_chars as word-internal, preserving combining marks and multi-codepoint names. These boundaries are baked into patterns during collection rather than patched up afterward. get_entity_patterns merges patterns from multiple locales, deduplicating list fields while preserving order, unioning stopwords, and caching results by canonical language tuple so case variants share one cache entry. Only zh-CN, hi, and ko ship full entity sections; other locales reuse English entity detection. For semantic retrieval, the embedding subsystem offers two ChromaDB-compatible embedding functions. The default minilm (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) is English-only and faster. The optional EmbeddinggemmaONNX wraps a 300MB quantized embeddinggemma-300m model supporting 100+ languages, lazy-loaded from HuggingFace on first use, achieving 0.88 cross-lingual cosine similarity versus MiniLM's 0.35. It truncates its 768-dim output to 384-dim via Matryoshka Representation Learning so it drops into existing collections without schema migration, and L2-normalizes. Because ChromaDB persists the embedding function name on each collection, switching models requires a rebuild-index. Device resolution via _resolve_providers maps cpu, cuda, coreml, dml, and auto to ONNX Runtime providers with CPU fallback and one-shot warnings. The Dialect class loads locale-specific AAAK instructions and regex to guide lossy compression. Configuration reads entity_languages and embedding_model to select which languages apply and whether to use multilingual embeddings.
